title: Control Print Ltd-$ - 522295 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Control Print FY26 consolidated operating revenue rose to INR482 crores from INR425 crores; CP Italy (V-Shapes) packaging losses remain the key concern.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total revenue of INR484 crores (vs INR431 crores) and standalone Q4 total revenue of about INR138 crores (vs INR114 crores). Standalone coding and marking drove growth, with management attributing most of the increase to volume and a small part to price, and a surcharge introduced to offset input cost pressure. The call was dominated by questions on losses at the Italian subsidiary V-Shapes (CP Italy), which management attributed almost entirely to the packaging business, and on the rationale for new IP and track-and-trace investments. Management said V-Shapes losses should fall in FY27 and could approach breakeven, though no firm timeline was given.

financial_highlights.value: rose from about INR21 crores to INR27-28 crores (analyst's figures, not disputed by management)

segments.name: Coding and marking (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management calls it the main profit centre; Q4 revenue mix was printers 12%, consumables 62%, spares 9%, services 16%. FY26 mix was printers 14%, consumables 61%, spares 9%, services 15%. Management expects a reasonably good year in FY27.

segments.name: Track and Trace
segments.commentary: Management says the conventional business is at breakeven or slightly profitable; no figures disclosed. Two pilots with top 5-10 Indian pharma companies are nearing completion, with a possible scale-up if results succeed.

segments.name: Packaging (India and overseas)
segments.commentary: Management cited good traction in core packing, with a pipeline for laminates, food packing and new machines. A new UNNATI packaging-material plant is planned at Guwahati to lower material costs.

segments.name: CP Italy / V-Shapes (packaging machines)
segments.commentary: Management says the subsidiary accounts for almost all consolidated overseas losses. Loss for FY26 was guided at about EUR1.5 million, down from EUR2-2.5 million in FY25. Machine quality issues and the inability to ship machines to Gulf customers have delayed revenue.

segments.name: CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT
segments.commentary: Management says these are at breakeven or better, with 15-20% growth expected for each; CODEOLOGY is being restructured to a smaller core business, and MARKPRINT has contracts in hand. No subsidiary-level sales or profit figures were disclosed.

guidance_outlook: V-Shapes losses expected to reduce in FY26/FY27, with breakeven possible this year per management; no firm commitment.

Management said no further major equity infusion into V-Shapes is needed after the current IP and inventory conversion, though a planned EUR-denominated IP and equity infusion of about INR32 crores into the Italian subsidiary was raised by an analyst.
CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT expected to grow about 15-20% a year.
Surcharge to customers to continue until the end of the calendar year to offset cost increases.

Guwahati UNNATI plant to cut packaging material costs by about 40% (from about INR2-2.5 per pack to about INR1.5 or lower) and is supported by incentives including INR7.5 crores capital subsidy, 5% interest subvention for six years and GST refund over 10 years.
capex_capacity: Guwahati UNNATI packaging-material plant planned in the Northeast, for which management cited incentives: a capital subsidy of INR7.5 crores on a INR15 crore plant and machinery investment (capped), 5% interest subvention for six years, and a GST refund over 10 years equal to plant and machinery investment.
CP Italy batch of 10 machines being finalized; first two machines had quality and specification issues, and the company is supplying stock machines from India to customers in the interim.
Management says V-Shapes is sourcing parts from local Italian suppliers at higher cost and plans to move sourcing to India to reduce costs in batches.
Print-and-apply and thermal transfer print engine being developed under CODEOLOGY; first sales expected in FY27.
Management said Guwahati expansion uses existing plot and is a minor expansion in an existing plant with spare capacity.
demand_pricing: Management said price hikes were implemented and a customer surcharge was introduced to recover input costs; the price hike size was not quantified.
Management attributed the Q4 standalone growth mainly to volume, with some cost-driven price increases.

Management said the Indian coding and marking market is about INR2,000-2,200 crores, growing about 10% a year, and that packaging-sector (pharma, F&B, FMCG) demand is stable while industrial demand fluctuates more.
Gulf and Middle East customers of V-Shapes stopped buying as shipments to the Strait of Hormuz area were blocked.

Management said the Track and Trace market is about INR500-600 crores, and that pharma serialization (top 300 drugs, possibly extended to 946) is a driver, though there is no notification yet on the extension.

qa_highlights.question: Keshav Garg: Are the international acquisition losses a repeat of past vanity acquisitions, and what are the cumulative loss and capital invested?
qa_highlights.answer: Shiva Kabra said the losses are almost entirely in the overseas packaging business (CP Italy) and that the programme has milestones; the investment cycle is longer than expected because the machines needed more stabilisation. He said the IP is now held by Control Print rather than CP Italy and could be licensed. No cumulative loss or investment figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Madhur Rathi: What drove the rise in standalone employee benefit expense from about INR21 crores to INR27-28 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep Barve said the new wage code (effective November 2025) required a recast of leave-encashment and gratuity liabilities, about INR3.5 crores in impact. Provisions were also made for sales incentives and key management loyalty bonuses.

qa_highlights.question: Vinit Thakur: When will V-Shapes break even, and will losses stop after FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said V-Shapes losses were about EUR2-2.5 million in FY25 and were guided to about EUR1.5 million this year; breakeven could come this year. He said little further funding is needed after current inventory ships, though some loans to V-Shapes will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What are the nature of the losses and the course correction for V-Shapes?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said about half of V-Shapes costs are R&D, and the rest is contract packaging plus manufacturing and sales. Fixed operating costs were estimated at about USD2-2.5 million per year, with total costs of about EUR2-3 million. Three to four non-productive staff have been let go; investment is going into sales.

qa_highlights.question: Saloni Arya: When do losses subside, what is the Track and Trace market size and margin, and what is the V-Shapes investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said the Track and Trace market is about INR500-600 crores; pilots are with two large pharma companies. He said margins are at least similar to the coding and marking gross margin, with no numerical margin disclosed. No cumulative V-Shapes investment was given.

qa_highlights.question: Samarth Singh: Where are the quality issues at CP Italy, and what is the total cost base?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said the first machines needed multiple engineering visits and the second was swapped for stock, so the company is aiming for 10 identical machines. Jaideep Barve said the CP Italy total cost is about EUR750,000 a year in direct wages, and Kabra said total fixed operating cost is about USD2-2.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Nikunj Bhanushali: What were the FY26 sales and P&L of CODEOLOGY, MARKPRINT and CP Italy, and what growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose subsidiary sales or profit figures; said the entire consolidated overseas loss is CP Italy. Kabra guided CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT to 15-20% growth and said CODEOLOGY will be scaled down for margin. FY26 printer sales were about 3,064.

risks_watch: CP Italy losses and machine quality: whether the 10-machine batch ships and the order backlog clears, and whether losses fall in H2 FY27 as guided.
Potential further capital infusion into CP Italy (analyst cited about INR32 crores) and the cumulative investment, which management did not quantify.
Input-cost pressure from the Middle East conflict and rupee depreciation, and whether the customer surcharge holds to year-end.
Gulf and Middle East shipments blocked, affecting CP Italy revenue.
Track and Trace pilot conversion with two large pharma companies and the timing of any government extension of the serialization list to 946 drugs.
Employee costs rising to 23% of consolidated operating revenue, partly from the wage code impact.
Limited subsidiary-level disclosure: management declined to share CODEOLOGY, MARKPRINT and CP Italy sales or profit.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core coding and marking business and on the long-term IP strategy, but defensive and evasive on the timing and size of CP Italy losses, track-and-trace economics and cumulative investment. Management often deferred numerical answers to later or to the annual report.
key_quotes: There's no vanity here. We're not taking on certain things. It's a very calculative decision.
So it could be this year also.
I don't think that we need to put more funds in after this -- since we purchased the technology and shipped it to India.
Now it's running fine. The second machine we had to sell to a customer in India.
I think that's what one would expect there in both CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT.
In general, whatever we do in terms of any business is at a similar gross margin level to what we do in our coding and marking business, at least.

adds.what: Guwahati UNNATI packaging-material plant (Northeast), INR15 crore plant and machinery investment, cuts packaging material cost ~40%
CP Italy (V-Shapes) batch of 10 packaging machines being finalized; first two had quality issues

growth.why: Management expects a reasonably good FY27 for standalone coding and marking, with CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT guided at 15-20% growth and V-Shapes losses cut to about EUR1.5m, but no firm revenue guidance was given and backing is partial (Guwahati plant, pilots, surcharge, and CP Italy machine batch rather than contracted orders).
